description: The ONE versioned rich-text sanitizer allowlist (design spec §5, sanitizer contract). bluemonday (apps/server, write-path sanitization before a rich-text field is stored) and DOMPurify (apps/web, client-render-path re-sanitization — see packages/schema/README.md's bullet on this file and hostile-corpus.json) must both be configured to accept exactly this set of tags, attributes, and URL schemes, and both WILL BE conformance-tested against packages/schema/validation/hostile-corpus.json once wired (phase-gate review finding M3: at Phase 0, neither sanitizer exists yet in apps/ — grep finds no bluemonday/DOMPurify reference anywhere; the allowlist and corpus data artifacts are P0, the actual sanitizer wiring and hostile-corpus neutralization are P3/AC-SEC-001, per docs/plans/traceability/ac-sec.md's AC-SEC-001/AC-SEC-003 rows — this file only pins the DATA both will be tested against, not a claim that the testing already runs). resume.schema.json's sanitizerAllowlistVersion const pins which version of this file a given schemaVersion's documents were sanitized against; #/$defs/link's pattern hardcodes urlSchemes below for structured (non-HTML) URL fields, since JSON Schema cannot itself parse HTML to check tags/attributes — that half of this file only constrains bluemonday/DOMPurify, not resume.schema.json.

forbidden.description: Explicitly called out (not exhaustive — anything not in tags/attributes above is already rejected by construction): design spec §5 names these as forbidden outright.

linkHardening.description: Every emitted <a> gets rel="noopener noreferrer" regardless of what (if anything) the source HTML specified — design spec §5.
